The maximum negative torque value, about −230 [Nm], is 4.15 multiple of the nominal torque value, which is realistic. When a required current frequency fcr is given and we look for the fvr voltage frequency that fulfills that task, Eq. (17) becomes an ordinary differential equation that can be applied to solve the inverse problem: d/dt(fvr · t) + fvr = fcr.
The solution of (21) takes the following form fvr = (1/t) ∫ fcr(τ)dτ + c/t, where c is an arbitrary constant and the lower limit of the integral can take the form of any nonzero value.

The maximum value of speed is about 1550 (rev/min), while the synchronous speed at 50 (Hz) is equal to 1000 (rev/min). According to (18), which concerns linear voltage frequency increase, the final fc frequency in the presented case should be 80 (Hz), which gives 1600 (rev/min) speed of the magnetic field rotation.

Generally, this example shows that the linear frequency increase is not the best option, due to the considerable current frequency overshoot and a substantial dynamic disruption after the point of the sharp frequency slope change. It seems that the best option should be exponential voltage frequency increase, being a soft curve of change. However, this example does not include any rotor speed regulation during starting course, acting on the voltage frequency curve, which can introduce substantial difference in the operation of the drive.

In a single phase system this does not mean that the frequency is negative, as it just passes zero and changes phase. But in the three phase system negative frequency means change of sequence of phases.
